News.title: Eight released over alleged threat to Islamic event
News.content:
Eight more people have been freed from custody, as police continue to investigate an alleged extreme right-wing threat to an Islamic event in Suffolk.

Officers became aware of the threat to the UK Ijtima event at Shrubland Hall, near Ipswich, last weekend.

Thousands of people attended the gathering but it closed early on police advice.

The Metropolitan Police said on Saturday, external that seven men were released from custody without charge, while another man was released on bail with strict conditions pending further inquiries.

The force said the investigation involved searching homes and vehicles, and more than 35 digital devices were seized.

Following those searches, a 42-year-old man was charged with two counts of possession of offensive weapons, extendable batons, and possession of a stun gun.

Police said the charges were not believed to be connected to the alleged threat on UK Ijtima.

The man was remanded in custody to appear at Reading Magistrates' Court on Monday.

Four other people were previously released on bail pending further inquiries.

News.title: Lib Dems urge FA and Uefa to withdraw from Fifa
News.content:
The relationship between Uefa and Fifa has been tense during the World Cup, with the governing bodies clashing over the Folarin Balogun incident and other issues.

Uefa, Europe's football governing body, said the decision not to uphold Balogun's ban had "crossed a red line", branding it "unprecedented, incomprehensible and unjustifiable".

Fifa has faced criticism for the high cost of tickets to watch World Cup matches under its dynamic pricing system, and its response to Somali referee Omar Artan being denied entry to the US to officiate at the tournament.

The Liberal Democrats said these examples showed Fifa was "too far gone".

Infantino defended ticket costs, arguing they were in line with other US sporting events.

There are 211 national football associations that are full members of Fifa, which organises the World Cup.

The English FA is a member of Fifa and if it withdrew from the governing body, England would not be able to compete in the World Cup.

Sir Ed said football associations should work together "to build a clean, transparent governing body that puts fans first".

The "only route forward is for the FA, along with other European governing bodies, to lead a co-ordinated exit from Fifa", he added.

Infantino has "crossed red line after red line", Sir Ed says, accusing him of "allowing corporate greed to exploit fans at will, destroying the integrity of the beautiful game".

"It is time for Uefa to step up and walk away from Fifa, and start working with other confederations to build a clean, transparent governing body that puts fans first."

Football Action Network, a campaign group for football organisations, said there does need to be a debate about Fifa's future.

"Nothing should be off the table if the game's global governing body refuses to reform," said Niall Couper, chair of the Football Action Network

Infantino's presidency of Fifa has been controversial since he was elected to lead the governing body in 2016.

Supporters argue he has expanded the game and increased funding for member associations.

Critics say he has centralised power, prioritised commercial growth at the expense of fan experience, and weakened governance standards.

He is widely expected to have enough support from football associations to secure a fourth term as president, extending his tenure until 2031.

Anna Sabine MP, Liberal Democrat Spokesperson for Culture, Media and Sport said Fifa behaves "more like a closed-shop cartel than a neutral global sporting body".

She said: "By rubber-stamping a fourth term despite these toxic scandals, football's governing bodies are showing they are content to sit in rotten squalor rather than strive for something better.

"Fans deserve transparency and integrity, not another four years of unchecked cronyism," Sabine added.

News.title: 'My buyers dropped their offer by £15,000 the day before exchange': Gazundering and how to avoid it
News.content:
Sarah was excitedly packing up to move out of the terraced house her family had outgrown to a four-bedroom home in the countryside.

But the day before exchanging contracts the buyers of her house dropped their agreed offer by Â£15,000. "It was awful, your heart just drops to your stomach," says Sarah, not her real name.

She had fallen victim to gazundering, a rare but growing problem in the property market in England and Wales, according to the Conveyancing Association, external.

It is calling for government reforms aimed at tackling this and other house buying and selling issues to be brought in "without delay" instead of 2029 as planned.

For Sarah, her husband and two children their move had all been going smoothly.

They were selling the three-bedroom terrace they'd renovated and buying her parents' four-bedroom detached house in the countryside.

But the day before contracts were exchanged Sarah received a phone call from her "befuddled" estate agent saying he had some bad news.

Their buyers said they'd done some more research about the area and would now offer Â£15,000 less than the price they'd agreed.

"I can't even begin to go through the financial consequences [if we lost the sale]," she says.

If they accepted the lower offer they would be out of pocket but if they refused there would be costs too.

"We had already paid one set of legal fees but would have had to pay again if we needed a new buyer. We'd also paid the removal fees already and would have to pay again if we cancelled the moving date," says Sarah.

The final for the 2026 World Cup has been confirmed as holders Argentina prepare to defend their crown against Spain.

Spain overcame France in Dallas to book their place in the showpiece decider as they look to add global glory to the continental crown won at Euro 2024.

They were then joined by Argentina, who came from behind to break England hearts in stoppage time, a match that saw Thomas Tuchel’s substitute strategy backfire spectacularly.

Saturday pitched France and England, the two semi-final losers, against each other in a wild third place play-off, which the Three Lions won 6-4.

Then on Sunday, New Jersey will stage the final showpiece with kick-off at 8pm BST.

Here’s the full tournament bracket:

And here is every knockout fixture’s date, kick-off time and host city:

The World Cup began in Mexico City’s Azteca Stadium, the site of Diego Maradona’s most famous and infamous goals against England at the 1986 World Cup.

It was also the venue for two classic World Cup finals: Brazil’s win over Italy in 1970 which included Carlos Alberto’s iconic team goal to cap a 4-1 win; and Argentina’s 3-2 win over West Germany in 1986, where Jorge Burruchaga grabbed an 84th-minute winner.

The World Cup 2026 final is drawing closer with Spain booking their place in Sunday’s match in New Jersey after a fine display to beat France 2-0.

England battle Argentina in tonight’s other semi-final in Atlanta to decide the other finalist.

But Fifa President Gianni Infantino has modernised the tournament with influence from its co-hosts United States and the way some of its biggest sporting events operate, including the Super Bowl in the NFL.

This will mean a half-time show appealing to more forms of culture and new fans.

Here’s everything you need to know about the Fifa World Cup 2026 final half-time show:

When and where is the half-time show?

The half-time show will be on Sunday, 19 July 2026 at New York New Jersey Stadium, USA, the location for the final match, with kick-off set at 8pm BST (3pm ET), the half-time show is due to start from 8:50pm BST (3:50pm ET), with stoppage time and additional time to set up the stage and infrastructure perhaps leading to a start time after 9pm BST (4pm ET).

open image in gallery A view of MetLife Stadium in New Jersey ( AFP/Getty )

How long will the half-time show last?

Sources tell the Independent that the show will be around 20 minutes. There is the prospect of the usual 15-minute half-time break, followed by the planned 11-minute show, with Infantino emphasising the figure is inspired by 11 players on the pitch for each team.

Due to the laws of the game, governed by Ifab (the International Football Association Board), it is understood half-time breaks should “not exceed15 minutes,” but Sunday is due to break that law.

There is a precedent set from last year’s Club World Cup final between eventual winners Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain, which was also organised by Fifa and held in the same venue in New Jersey. That show lasted 24 minutes, with Coldplay, J Balvin, Doja Cat, Tems and Emmanuel Kelly featuring.

open image in gallery Tems, Doja Cat, Emmanuel Kelly, Chris Martin of Coldplay and J Balvin perform during the halftime show during the FIFA Club World Cup 2025 Final ( Getty )

Where can I watch the half-time show?

The game is on both BBC and ITV in the UK, with ITV revealing that it will broadcast the entire World Cup half-time show at the New York New Jersey Stadium, as well as match analysis.

The BBC will confirm its plans in the coming hours. Alternatively you can follow The Independent’s coverage in our live blog, which will be packed with updates from the show and reaction from social media and our reporters in the stadium.

Who is performing at the half-time show?

The 11-minute Super Bowl-style show will be co-headlined by Madonna, Shakira and K-pop boy band BTS.

Justin Bieber was added to the bill, while Burna Boy, Gustavo Dudamel and the PS22 Chorus featuring Coldplay also involved, and Chris Martin has curated the show.

open image in gallery Singer Shakira and her sons Sasha and Milan in the stand during Argentina v Austria ( Reuters )

Is there a closing ceremony and how is performing?

The closing ceremony starts at 18:30 BST (1:30pm ET), with the show including Tom Cruise, Laura Pausini, Nicole Scherzinger, Robbie Williams and IShowSpeed. And Jennifer Hudson is to sing the United States' national anthem.

A Chinese conglomerate that formerly owned British Steel is demanding compensation from the UK government for investment losses after the steelmaker's nationalisation last week.

The UK government took operational control last year after Jingye Group considered closing its Scunthorpe plant's blast furnaces.

In a WeChat statement, Jingye claimed the nationalisation "tarnished the credibility of the British government, spooked international investors and caused great losses to the company’s operation and British taxpayers' funds." It also demanded the UK government cease "trampling on international investment rules."

The firm has initiated negotiation procedures under bilateral investment agreements, reserving all rights. Jingye stated it would also represent taxpayers seeking to hold the UK government and Steel’s management legally liable, though specifics remain undisclosed.

“The U.K. disregarded Jingye's continuous investment and significant contribution and was only willing to provide almost zero compensation,” it said.

Jingye claimed the nationalisation ‘tarnished the credibility of the British government, spooked international investors and caused great losses to the company’s operation and British taxpayers' funds’ ( Getty )

An independent evaluation will be carried out to determine whether any compensation will be paid to Jingye Group, the U.K. government said last week.

The Department for Business and Trade announced the move on July 17, saying it would save thousands of jobs and protect the U.K.’s national interest by ensuring a supply of domestically produced steel for major construction projects and the defense industry.

British Steel and its forebears have been making steel at Scunthorpe for more than 130 years, building on the U.K.’s development of improved steelmaking technology during the Industrial Revolution. The plant currently employs about 2,700 people.

Jingye bought British Steel in 2020 and said it saved the steel company from crisis.

The Chinese Foreign Ministry on Saturday said the way the U.K. handles the issue would directly influence how Chinese investors view the British investment environment and the credibility of the British government.

“China urges the UK to earnestly respect market principles and the spirit of contract, and find solutions on compensation and other issues acceptable to both sides,” it said in a statement.

It added China supports enterprises in safeguarding their legitimate rights through legal means.

Slovenian referee Slavko Vincic will officiate the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina on Sunday.

Vincic will be joined by compatriot assistants Tomaz Klancnik and Andraz Kovacic, making history as the first ever referee from Slovenia to take charge of the landmark fixture.

“So, first of all, a shock. Then happiness. I was shaking, so it’s an incredible honour to get the World Cup final,” said Vincic, who was in tears upon hearing the news. “It’s something that… it’s only a dream for a referee, for a young referee when they start. So, I’m very proud, very proud of myself, my team.

Slavko Vincic will take charge of the World Cup final ( Getty )

“It’s very difficult to put everything into words, but I’m very proud to represent my country, Slovenia, in the biggest sporting event in the world. So, yeah, I’m very proud. My team is very proud and we will do our best.”

Vincic is no stranger to the elite game and is highly experienced at the very top level of European football.

He officiated the 2024 Champions League final between Real Madrid and Borussia Dortmund at Wembley, two years after taking charge of the Europa League final that pitted Rangers and Eintracht Frankfurt against each other.

The 46-year-old has refereed at two European Championships, overseeing Spain’s Euro 2024 semi-final win over France on their journey to becoming champions.

Vincic made his World Cup debut in Qatar in 2022, with his first match bringing back bad memories for Argentina. He took charge of their shock opening loss to Saudi Arabia, something Lionel Scaloni’s side managed to of course bounce back from as they went on to win the tournament.

Sunday’s finale will mark his sixth career World Cup match overall and his fourth assignment of the current campaign, which kicked off during the group stage with Brazil’s 1-1 draw with Morocco.

He also officiated Algeria’s group-stage win over Jordan before overseeing co-hosts Mexico’s last-32 triumph against fellow dark horses Ecuador.

A story that has surprised fans this week has been the news that Vincic was once wrongly arrested at a “sex party” in Bosnia in 2020, per The Sun. Vincic told Slovenian media he was attending a business lunch when a raid took place and drugs, guns and money were seized. He was later probed by police as a witness before being released, with law enforcement deciding he had nothing to do with the incident.

Vincic later told Slovenian media: “I found myself on this ranch by chance. I have my own company, I was in Bosnia and Herzegovina for a business meeting. I accepted an invitation to lunch, which turned out to be my biggest mistake. I regret it. I was sitting at a table with my company, all of a sudden the police came and what happened, happened. I have nothing to do with the group that was arrested and detained, nor do my business partners. Yes, they really took us to the police, asked [us] as witnesses, when it turned out that we didn’t even know them, we were able to go.”

Slovenian refereeing boss Vlado Sajn added: “According to the information we gathered from official and unofficial sources, and last but not least from Slavko himself, he is not suspected of anything, no proceedings have been instituted against him. He found himself in this place at the wrong time. He was invited to a party where there was a large group of people – he did not know the vast majority… I consider this story to be a web of unfortunate circumstances.”

The race for the golden boot at the World Cup is heading for a thrilling climax featuring some of the best players in the world.

The superstars have lived up their hype at this tournament, none more so than France’s Kylian Mbappe and Argentina hero Lionel Messi. Both have gone tit for tat since the very first outing, each storming past poor Miroslav Klose’s all-time goalscoring record to enter the semi-finals with eight goals apiece. Mbappe’s double in the so-called bronze final took him ahead of Messi, who will have the chance to answer as he faces Spain in the showpiece decider.

But in a twist an already enthralling race, team success may prove a detriment to Messi’s hopes. He is the only real contender for the accolade in the final and faces a tough challenge of breaching Spain’s rock-solid defence, which has only conceded once this tournament. If players are tied for goals, the number of assists will determine who ranks higher. If there is still a tie, it comes down to minutes played and the goals-per-minute ratio, which would favour Mbappe over Messi provided the Argentina captain plays the full final, if it got that far.

The talismanic pair are now the only players in the hunt – though England duo Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham both finish highly. Bellingham went ahead of Erling Haaland with his seventh goall as he finished off a 6-4 win against France to secure a third place finish.

News.title: Tuchel learns lesson as England clinch third place in 10-goal thriller
News.content:
Neither England nor France wanted to be playing this game in Miami, but they can have no complaints about the nature of their semi-final defeats.

Tournament favourites France were comprehensively outplayed by Spain, with their feted front four of Kylian Mbappe, Ousmane Dembele, Bradley Barcola and Michael Olise all turning in below-par performances.

England’s defeat by Argentina was perhaps not as much of a surprise, but the nature of Thomas Tuchel’s team’s second-half collapse was just as alarming as France’s no-show.

England’s manager was fiercely criticised for replacing Anthony Gordon with Ezri Konsa and switching to a back five in the 72nd minute, but Tuchel has since defended his decisions.

“If you are asking if I regret my decisions, if this is the question, then I say no. I don’t regret my ‌decisions because I ‌felt that we became ⁠too passive,” said Tuchel.

“I took several decisions, trusting my instinct, my intuition, my experience, trusting my competitiveness, and I took the decision in order to help the team and get the result.

“I would regret if I didn’t help. I would regret ⁠if we didn’t react, but I have no regrets over the decision itself.”

Quite how strong Didier Deschamps and Tuchel decide to go with their teams is anyone’s guess. There has been some suggestion that Mbappe will start to give him the chance to beat Lionel Messi to the Golden Boot.

Some of England’s regular starters, such as Declan Rice, look physically spent, so there could be some rotation, and even a chance for players such as Kobbie Mainoo who has not played a minute of football at the tournament.

The third/fourth-place play-off has been rebranded as the “Bronze Final” for this tournament, and Tuchel was keen to point out that finishing third would be England’s best World Cup result since 1966. They lost this fixture against Belgium in 2018, but the way that game has been widely forgotten speaks volumes.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: England win gives Borthwick breathing space after late try controversy
News.content:
And in doing so he may have just saved Borthwick’s job.

The Rugby Football Union, following its review into England’s Six Nations campaign that yielded just one victory, had publicly offered its backing to its head coach through to the World Cup. But in reality, there are no cast guarantees. It needed evidence of England’s progress.

Two wins from three rounds of the Nations Championship is likely to convince RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney to back his man. But Borthwick will know that nothing can be taken for granted.

Four years ago, Eddie Jones, facing similar scrutiny from his employers, looked to have salvaged his job by winning the last two matches in a three-Test summer tour of Australia. But it did still not save him from the sack the following November.

Still. There was enough character and attacking prowess to convince the RFU that despite the flaws in this display, the team are on the right track again.

It was still far from an 80-minute performance, but this was England’s first away victory in a year, in a hostile environment and after all the challenges, both physical and mental, the players have faced in travelling to three continents over three weeks – over 25,000 miles – at the end of a long season.

England wobbled alarmingly earlier in the second half but remarkably found the resilience to drag themselves back into the game just as it looked like it was slipping from their grasp. That is clear evidence of players playing for their coach and each other.

Discipline, however, remains a major problem for Borthwick’s England. They had been cruising to what would looked to have been a statement victory at half-time following tries by Tommy Freeman and two by Ben Earl in what had been their finest half of rugby this year.

And yet, once again indiscipline undermined their efforts. Remarkably they were shown four yellow cards – Jack van Poortvliet, Alex Coles, Pollock (to more booing) and Emmanuel Iyogun – in the second half to take their total to 14 in their last 10 Tests, and at one stage were down to 12 men but significantly this time it did not prove fatal. Just.

News.title: Scotland fight back to claim victory against Fiji in Nations Championship
News.content:
A barrelling Schoeman finished an initial break by match captain Stafford McDowall, then Dobie burrowed over beside the posts in the 61st minute to put Scotland in front for the first time in 40 minutes.

Scotland glossed up the scoreline with two more tries in the last six minutes by Cummings and Dobie again to send home a crowd of 55,000 happy.

“I thought our bench did really well,” Townsend told the BBC. “Something I’ve learned over the last 12 months, the bench can help you change momentum. The players can come up with solutions themselves but the bench can give you energy and solutions but also bravery. We’re a team that will back our decisions and that put real pressure on Fiji.

“I felt [Fiji] picked their strongest side today and it took a lot of work for us to break them down but also it took a really good defensive performance,” Townsend added. “Fiji didn’t really break us that often [and] in that final quarter the guys were outstanding. We’ll take a few positives from that.”

Fiji had never beaten Scotland at Murrayfield but would have sensed the chance of making history by half-time. The Fijians were tough and clinical in a huge turnaround from last weekend when they were humiliated by England 73-8 in Liverpool.

News.title: Hometown hero Tommy Fleetwood facing tough ask to end 57 years of Open hurt
News.content:
Never mind Bryson DeChambeau stomping around in the rough as he improved his lie, for so long this Open Saturday turned into Tommy Fleetwood walking in his Royal Birkdale wonderland as he enhanced the mood of seemingly everyone in attendance.

Alas, the fun could not last and, even though he still has a chance of becoming England’s first Open winner on English soil since 1969, that finish looked costly. Fifty-seven years of hurt and all that...

On five under, Fleetwood is in a tie for ninth, five off the lead held by Sam Burns, the American who, after a 65, is two clear of New Zealander Ryan Fox and South Korean Kim Si-woo. DeChambeau is alongside Swede Ludvig Aberg, in a tie for sixth on six under, after a 69.

He was heckled on the 18th because of the two-shot penalty he received on Friday night for “inadvertently improving his lie” on the fifth. “You’re a cheat, Bryson,” the fan shouted.

It was a sour point that was in no way in keeping with the mood of this Saturday that had been overwhelmingly positive. With Fleetwood as the focus, of course.

The enormous crowd cheered and sang and backed their fellow Merseysider all the way as Fleetwood launched his charge into contention at this Southport links which he would once sneak on as a child. His playing partner, Jon Rahm, was taken aback by the level of support.

“The best way I can explain it, it was so intense that, without meaning any disrespect I’m glad England didn’t win the semi-final [of the World Cup] because I would have been having a heck of a three days with the fans if they had been playing Spain in tomorrow’s final,” Rahm said.

News.title: Sloppy Springboks still strong enough to pulverise Wales
News.content:
If one image summed up South Africa’s complete control, it was in the 12th minute when Wales had a scrum on their own five-metre line. When the Springbok shove came, the Welsh pack went backwards like they were on roller-skates. The poor Welsh front row are going to have to check under their beds for snarling Springboks props for quite a few sleepless nights to come.

Wales’ best period of the game came just after the Springboks’ fourth try when they had three line-outs and took three tap penalties deep inside the South Africa 22. It amounted to absolutely nothing.

You can point fingers at head coach Steve Tandy’s selections and preparation if you wish, but there was little he could have done to change the result. It was only the manner of their hammering, he could have potentially affected.

Wales are not alone in this. Scotland and England may have posed a few more problems but they were still dispatched with ease. South Africa are truly in a league of their own, although New Zealand’s resurgence under Dave Rennie should at least provide a serious level of competition that the British mainland failed to provide.

In truth the best thing that Tandy could do is burn the tapes and hope that this is consigned to the deepest recesses of their collective memory. Tighthead Dillon Lewis especially may need one of those Men in Black memory wipers.

If you squinted hard enough, there were a couple of positives: the maul defence and high-ball contest. They were at least competitive. Aaron Wainwright had the unenviable job of packing down at the back of a retreating Welsh scrum but did a heroic job in the circumstances. Jac Morgan, too, was bravery personified in attacking the breakdown with the ferocity of the Springboks clean-out operation.

But in the infrequent periods when South Africa got on a roll without knocking on, there was precious little Wales could do to stop the green wave. The first try was a case in point. Emanating from a loose kick from Tomos Williams, full-back Aphelele Fassi broke the first line of Wales’ defence and then they kept coming through Cobus Wiese, Damien de Allende before Jasper Wiese accelerated through Morgan’s tackle and over the line.

News.title: Santos impresses in first Man Utd appearance but cannot prevent defeat by Wrexham
News.content:
United were without the players who have featured at this summer’s World Cup – including new signing Youri Tielemans – as well as Benjamin Sesko, but Michael Carrick put out a strong starting XI in front of 20,000 spectators in the Finnish capital.

Santos, who became United’s first summer signing when he joined from Chelsea at the start of the week for an initial £48m, took his place at the base of midfield alongside Mason Mount.

Speaking just before the match, Michael Carrick had praised the 22-year-old’s attitude, saying: “He’s settled in really well, he’s a fantastic character. He’s buzzing to be here, you can see that.”

The Brazilian’s first involvement was to clear the ball away after Tom Heaton failed to gather under pressure from Smith seconds into the game.

Santos was left on his backside by Lewis O’Brien eight minutes in but the chance came to nothing for Wrexham as the flag went up. More encouraging was his sliding block on O’Brien moments later and he soon settled in, showing a good range of passing and winning several duels in a busy display.

However, Phil Parkinson’s side, who played their first pre-season friendly against Wisla Krakow in Poland last weekend, were looking brighter and threatened again when Bailey Cadamarteri nicked the ball off Ayden Heaven on the edge of the box before the defender recovered.

United’s first chance was a Joshua Zirkzee shot that fizzed wide in the 24th minute and they almost went ahead when Smith tried to clear a cornerm but instead sent a header on to his own crossbar in the 36th minute.

News.title: Russell fighting ‘with one hand behind my back’ as Antonelli takes Belgium GP pole
News.content:
Russell and Mercedes are not clueless about his woes. Russell believes he is losing the bulk of the time on the straights, though Toto Wolff, the team principal, conceded that some time is also being lost in the corners. They are both, however, struggling to explain why he is haemorrhaging time in the flat-out sections of a track that is replete with them. It was the same at Silverstone, when Russell repeatedly bemoaned his power deficit to Antonelli and the other Mercedes-powered cars.

Heading into this weekend, Russell believed that these issues were down to Antonelli’s driving style leading to better battery deployment on the straights. “That’s what we thought coming out of Silverstone. We thought it was in the driving style and technique, but we have finally concluded it’s not. We have changed everything... it’s frustrating,” he said.

“So we keep going through this process of ‘Oh, we think it’s this’. We change it. ‘Oh, it’s not this, maybe it’s the driving style’. I thought it was the driving style. Honestly, I came into this weekend and said on Thursday, ‘I think it’s the driving style’. Changed the driving style, and it’s not the driving style.”

“Anything can happen [in the race]. But as I said, the truth is battling against my team-mate, who is such an incredible driver, doing such a great job at the moment, in the best of times, is a tall order.

Sports.title: World’s first football-branded homes near completion with rooftop pitch, panoramic sea views and BLUE sand beach
Sports.content:
THE world’s first homes branded with a recognisable football club are almost complete.

Residents can enjoy a rooftop pitch, panoramic sea views and even a blue sand beach.



DAMAC Properties has just unveiled its latest delivery of branded homes where residents can play football on the roof.

Located in Dubai Maritime City, the apartments are part of Chelsea Residences by Damac, with this new tower being the sixth, and final, part of the luxury waterfront development.



Developed in partnership with Chelsea Football Club, demand has been high from both investors and end-users for a home in the huge development complex, with the project already seeing the first five towers sell out.

Popularity for the properties stem from the site’s first-class location, sea-view homes and Chelsea-branded lifestyle concept for residents.



The sixth tower, Tower C, is made up from a limited number of one, two and three-bedroom apartments.



Each is set with panoramic sea views and residents can explore a wide range of football-inspired amenities and well-being experiences.

Footie fans can even play a game high up in the sky at The Summit, the UAE’s only rooftop football pitch.

The complex also boasts a blue-sand beach in honour of Chelsea’s team colours as well as a Beach Club and Athlete Training Centre.

Prices start from AED2.56 million (£517,000), and begin with sizes of 827 sq ft.

DAMAC is currently running a launch deal for those looking to invest in its properties.



Buyers will be able to receive a discount on flats when bought in bulk and save when paying upfront.

Managing director of DAMAC Properties, Amira Sajwani, said: “Chelsea Residences by DAMAC brings together an iconic global football brand, a prime waterfront setting and DAMAC’s signature approach to luxury living.

“With the launch of the final tower, investors have a rare opportunity to be part of a distinctive seafront community defined by panoramic sea views, wellness-led amenities and a lifestyle inspired by performance, leisure and resort-style living.”

According to DAMAC, Dubai is leading the global branded residence market as of 2025, with a yearly increase of 26 per cent in transaction volumes and a 51 per cent rise in transaction value.

The branded residence sector can draw a premium of up to 64 per cent in comparison with non-branded units.



Chelsea Residences by DAMAC highlights the luxury of branded properties, bringing together resort-like amenities and the name of one of the most recognisable football clubs.

DAMAC has delivered more than 500,000 homes and plans on constructing another 8,800 units in the emirate in 2026.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi fires World Cup final warning to Lamine Yamal and opens up on ‘crazy’ photo with Spain star
Sports.content:
LIONEL MESSI warned Lamine Yamal ahead of their superstar World Cup final showdown: “It’s not your time yet.”

The duo face off for the first time tonight as Argentina bid to become just the third nation to be crowned back-to-back champions.



Spain wonderkid Yamal, 19, was snapped with Messi as a five-month-old in 2007.

Eight-time Ballon d’Or winner Messi, 39, said: “That photo is crazy. He’s a tremendous player — a global star.



“He has this great opportunity to make history in this final. But of course we will give everything so that it’s not this time.”

Yamal was held by Messi after his parents won a charity photoshoot in Barcelona, where the young Spaniard now plays.

Inter Miami’s Messi added: “I had that photo with him when he was a baby. Facing each other now is incredible. He is a huge player I’ve followed a lot because he plays for a club I love.

“He’s one of the best in the world. He has his whole career ahead of him. But we will give our all to ensure he doesn’t become champion this time.”

Messi hopes to emulate Pele, who was part of the Brazil team that last retained the World Cup in 1962.

Spain skipper Rodri said: “What Messi means as a player and for Argentina goes beyond words. Obviously, for me, he’s the greatest of all time.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

“But Argentina is more than just Messi. They are a very complete team with top-tier players.”

Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni would not be drawn on whether tonight will be Messi’s final match of an extraordinary 20-year World Cup career.

He said: “What do I know? Ask him directly!

“I don’t have the foggiest idea. He doesn’t stop surprising us. Lionel is the best footballer the world has seen.

“Reaching a final at 39 is unbelievable. We miss Diego Maradona. Messi is still with us, so we need to enjoy him.”

Sports.title: Argentina keeper Emi Martinez playing with BROKEN FINGER and couldn’t even train at World Cup
Sports.content:
EMI MARTINEZ is playing through the pain barrier after breaking his finger just before the World Cup.

The Argentina goalkeeper, 33, did the damage during the Europa League final warm-up on May 20 before Aston Villa beat Freiburg in Istanbul.



The injury threatened to derail his World Cup.

But Martinez ignored advice to have an operation, battling through to play all seven matches in North America – even though he did not join in full training until after the last 16.



Previewing the MetLife final, the stopper said: “It still hurts. I knew that my hand was going to be hurting.

“I tried to avoid going through surgery. I consulted a great deal of hand specialists in England, the USA and other countries.



“Of course, after winning a final with a broken finger, you’re told you have to undergo surgery and that you’ll be missed for the entire group stage of a World Cup.

“At the beginning, I couldn’t even train with the Argentina team.

“So many questions come to mind. I had a different preparation from my team-mates.

“Two days before the first match, I wasn’t feeling good.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

“After Egypt, I was joining the training sessions normally, I stopped thinking about that and now I feel so much better.”

Martinez will be feeling so much better if he helps Argentina win a second straight World Cup.

He was a superstar in Qatar, especially with his 123rd-minute save to deny Randal Kolo Muani and final shootout stop from Kingsley Coman.

But despite his wind-up tactics and eccentricity, Martinez insists he is very happy to let others take the glory.

He added: “I’ve never wanted to be the protagonist.



“Truth be told, having the trophy for the best player is really not important for me.

“I don’t want to be making the headlines.

“My coach sent me a message, ‘I don’t mind about your condition, you will be in my team.’ That is more important for me than saving a penalty and making the headlines.



“I want my team-mates to be the stars. Goalkeepers are the only ones who don’t score goals and don’t celebrate.

“Pressure doesn’t weigh me down, whether I’m playing in my home Mar del Plata neighbourhood or in a final.

“I’m going to jump on the pitch with a smile.”

The World Cup final against Spain could see Martinez win five finals in five years with Argentina.

In 2018, he went to Russia as a fan.



In 2006, aged 13, it ended in tears in the quarter-finals.

Martinez reflected: “I cried when Jens Lehmann saved our penalties.

“I’ve always been a national team fan and always dreamt of reaching the national team.

“I am enjoying this World Cup much more than Qatar. I suffered a lot after Saudi Arabia scored twice to win. I made one save against Mexico, same with Austria.

“When Poland shot on target, it was in. Australia and the Netherlands shot twice and scored once.

“People said I had a more decisive role. Why? Maybe just because of the penalties.”

Few would bet against more Martinez heroics and headlines if he is called upon tonight.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel reveals he didn’t know England hero Bukayo Saka had scored World Cup hat-trick against France
Sports.content:
THOMAS TUCHEL confessed he did not realise Bukayo Saka had scored a hat-trick as England edged France in one of the craziest World Cup games ever.

The Three Lions sealed third place with a breathtaking 6-4 victory in Miami after racing into a 4-0 half-time lead before surviving a ferocious French fightback.



Saka was England’s star man, scoring twice before the break and completing his treble from the penalty spot late on after Djed Spence was brought down.

But despite the Arsenal winger’s heroics, Tuchel admitted he completely lost track of who had scored during the chaos.



He told BBC Sport: “Bukayo showed that he is a key player. There is never a doubt.”

Then came the surprise admission.

Tuchel said: “I wasn’t aware he had a hat-trick. I lost the overview of the goalscorers, but brilliant.”

Tuchel’s handling of Saka has been under the spotlight throughout the tournament, intensifying since the star wingers watched the whole of England’s semi-final capitulation against Argentina from the bench.

Fans and pundits had assumed Saka must have been unavailable for the game, having carried an injury earlier in the tournament.

But, speaking after his hat-trick heroics, the Gunners hero insisted he WAS fit and healthy.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

England had looked home and dry after first-half strikes from Declan Rice, Ezri Konsa and Saka’s double put them four goals clear.

France roared back through Kylian Mbappe’s brace and a Bradley Barcola goal, piling the pressure on Tuchel’s side.

But a Saka penalty in the 87th minute to complete his hat-trick settled England’s nerves, regardless of a deep stoppage-time goal from current Ballon d’Or winner Ousmane Dembele.

Jude Bellingham then responded just two minutes later in the 98th minute to seal the victory.



The midfielder’s seven goals at the 2026 World Cup are the most scored by any England men’s player at a major tournament.

Tuchel admitted his team needed fresh legs after the break as Les Bleus dominated possession.

He said: “Not sure if we had more control. We just had fresher legs and quality players again.

“The others were tired. France played in their full flow and full risk, so we got unlucky to not concede the equaliser and finish it off with a penalty and a brilliant goal.”

Saka’s hat-trick ultimately proved decisive as England signed off the tournament with the bronze medal – even if their own manager did not realise his winger had completed the feat until after the final whistle.

Sports.title: Lamine Yamal: Heartbreaking reason Spain star's dad won't attend World Cup final
Sports.content:
Lamine Yamal: Heartbreaking reason Spain star's dad won't attend World Cup final

Lamine Yamal is looking to outgun Lionel Messi in the World Cup final as Spain collide with Argentina for the biggest prize in football

View 2 Images Lamine Yamal with his dad Mounir Nasraoui after winning Euro 2024 with Spain

Lamine Yamal's father will not attend the World Cup final in person - as he hasn't been able to end any match all tournament.

‌



Mounir Nasraoui has revealed he did not feel fit to travel this summer due to his health. It means Nasraoui is set to cheer on the 19-year-old Barcelona superstar from home.

‌



He explained: "I'm an epileptic. I have to take a lot of medication every day, and I can have an epilepsy seizure.

‌



"I could be here, right now, under the effects of stress or emotion, and have a seizure without realising it. So you always have to think things through carefully.

"Before traveling, you have to think about me, about him, and about all the people around us, you know? I might end up causing problems. So it's better to stay home and watch all this from here."

Spain and Argentina World Cup final training plans rocked by electrical thunderstorms READ MORE :

Spain star Aymeric Laporte calls out Argentina over England World Cup antics READ MORE :

Around a month after Yamal's last major tournament, Euro 2024 - which he won, dad Mounir was stabbed in a parking lot. The authorities arrested four people in connection with the incident.

‌



He remains very close to his family despite his superstardom. His brother Keyne, who is three years old, has been one of the heroes of this World Cup due to his celebrations in the stands.

"I come from an apartment where the kitchen and the bedroom were the same space," Yamal recently stated, citing his humble beginnings.

"I see my mother happy, I see that my brother can have the childhood I would have liked to have, and that's what makes me happiest."

‌



View 2 Images Mounir Nasraoui, the father of Lamine Yamal, suffers with epilepsy

Fatima, Yamal's paternal grandmother, left Morocco on a bus that she wasn't legally allowed to board. She would work shifts just so her son could join before he ended up having Yamal as a teenager.

Now that 19-year-old is about to walk out on the biggest stage of all. While Yamal's parents split when he was three, his football career took off soon after.

‌



He joined Barcelona's youth ranks at seven, though he was actually scouted at the age of seven and at the age of 15, he made his big breakthrough into the first-team.

In doing so, he became the youngest player to make their debut for the Catalan giants since way back in 1922.

Yamal has scored just one goal at this World Cup but after shaking off a thigh issue, he is expected to start against Argentina as he looks to add a second international trophy to his cabinet.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel sets record straight on Bukayo Saka decision after England star speaks out
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel sets record straight on Bukayo Saka decision after England star speaks out

Bukayo Saka showed his worth by scoring a hat-trick in England's barnstorming 6-4 win against France to finish third at the World Cup, having started neither of their previous two matches

View 2 Images Thomas Tuchel revealed his thinking behind not using Bukayo Saka more (Image: Carmen Mandato - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

Thomas Tuchel has explained why Bukayo Saka was given a reduced role at the World Cup after the England star admitted that he wanted to play more. Arsenal star Saka scored a hat-trick in Saturday's third-place play-off against France, as the Three Lions ran out 6-4 winners following one of the wildest games in World Cup history.

‌



The winger became only the fourth male England player to score a hat-trick at a World Cup, matching the achievements of Sir Geoff Hurst, Gary Lineker and Harry Kane. But after coming into the tournament with an Achillies injury, Saka started just one of England's four knockout matches prior to beating France, and wasn't given a single minute in their late semi-final loss against Argentina.

‌



Post-match, Tuchel was asked why he didn't hand the 24-year-old a more prominent role. "He did everything right," the England manager acknowledged. "I just had the feeling in the semi-final for Morgan Rogers that he would be involved in something special, and that was it.

‌



"And then the game in itself demands so much, you're forced into changes because of cramps and the flow of the game so Bukayo showed he was a key player, it was never a doubt. I was not even aware he had a hat-trick, I lost the overview of all the goalscorers, but well-deserved credit."

Tuchel went on to say: "He was excellent, Bukayo is a key player for me. He was ready to go in the World Cup, I felt still the responsibility as a coach, and with the history given where he came from to take it slow with Bukayo.

"He started quite some matches, it was a tough decision for me to leave him out of the semi-final. I had a feeling after the Norway match that Morgan Rogers had something special to give to us with his physicality and his body in the match against Argentina.

"We had him warm up several times against Argentina, we were ready to change but the game became so crazy that in the end we opted for a different option.

‌



Should Bukayo Saka have started more at the World Cup? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Bukayo Saka made history with his hat-trick (Image: Luke Hales/Getty Images)

"But nothing has changed during this World Cup for me, Bukayo is a fantastic teammate, a fantastic football player, a key player for us, that will not change, he showed it again today, I'm happy for him and happy for us, he's excellent."

Saka, meanwhile, made it clear that he was disappointed with his lack of action, having declared that he was fit. "Of course I would love to have played more but it's too late to talk about that," he admitted. "I try to do my talking on the pitch and it's done now, move on."

Sports.title: Inside Lionel Messi vs Lamine Yamal World Cup final 19 years on from infamous bath picture
Sports.content:
Inside Lionel Messi vs Lamine Yamal World Cup final 19 years on from infamous bath picture

Lionel Messi and Lamine Yamal square off in the World Cup final on Sunday in New Jersey as Argentina bid to retain their crown against Spain - it's a generational storyline that defies all logic

View 3 Images Lionel Messi and Lamine Yamal collide in the World Cup final

Full circle doesn't quite cut it. If you do not believe in destiny, perhaps you will now. Nineteen years ago, inside the away dressing room at Barcelona's Camp Nou, the first brick in the long-winding road to the 2026 World Cup final was laid.

‌



Lamine Yamal's parents, mother Sheila Ebana from Equatorial Guinea and Moroccan-born father Mounir Nasraoui, optimistically entered a raffle published in Catalan newspaper Sport.

‌



The prize? A photoshoot with a mystery player from Barca's first-team. Not only was Yamal the lucky winner but he was also paired with future great Messi, who cradled and bathed the five-month-old superstar in the making.

‌



The famous shots, captured by snapper Joan Monfort, are so surreal they could be mistaken for artificial intelligence.

Just shy of two decades after being blessed by the GOAT, Yamal collides with his long-standing idol for a shot at World Cup glory in New Jersey. It's a script even the greatest fantasists will have struggled to write.

Spain and Argentina World Cup final training plans rocked by electrical thunderstorms READ MORE :

Spain star Aymeric Laporte calls out Argentina over England World Cup antics READ MORE :

At the time of the remarkable photographs, genius Messi was just 19. He had scored 11 career goals and had already won both La Liga and the Champions League.

‌



It was impressive but by comparison, Yamal, who coincidentally turned 19 on Monday, has blown that record out of the water.

The Spain wide gem has 56 goals to boot, won La Liga on three different occasions, and fired his country to European Championship supremacy in 2024.

Now he has the opportunity to move level with Messi regarding World Cup titles. It would cement his status as the heir to the 39-year-old icon's throne and represent a passing of the baton.

‌



Do not discount the veteran, however, from extending his illustrious legacy. He has scored eight goals at this World Cup alone, registered four assists and single-handedly dragged Argentina within touching distance of retaining the trophy.

View 3 Images The famous picture where Lionel Messi bathed five-month-old Lamine Yamal (Image: AP)

Before the dramatic midweek victory over England, Thomas Tuchel had described the irresistible forward as a silent killer.

‌



It was a fitting description as Messi has walked 47 per cent of the total distance he has covered at this tournament.

He is averaging 8.2km per 90 minutes, the shortest tally of all outfield team-mates that have played more than 20 minutes at this World Cup.

Messi has even had fewer touches (43) than Yamal (51) in the opposition box, underlining his predatory instincts in the final third.

‌



Both have made seven appearances and started six matches at this World Cup but Yamal has scored just once against Saudi Arabia and is yet to record an assist.

Meanwhile, the inspirational Argentina captain is averaging a goal involvement every 51 minutes, crushing his understudy.

Despite those statistics, victory for Spain would catapult Yamal's profile into a whole new stratosphere. Messi's stature speaks for itself but contrastingly, La Roja's fresh-faced teen has relished the opportunity to enjoy ordinary things outside of matches at this World Cup.

‌



View 3 Images Lionel Messi is eyeing back-to-back World Cups with Argentina (Image: Getty Images)

He was spotted shopping at Walmart in Fort Oglethorpe on the outskirts of Spain's Chattanooga training base earlier in the tournament while after the 2-0 semi-final scalp over France in Dallas, he strolled up to a street food stall in smoggy New York.

Yamal doesn't relish the limelight but if he triumphs in the World Cup final, the reality is, his life will quite simply never be the same again.

‌



Messi is striving to sign off in style in what could potentially yet prove to be his last dance and final act as an Argentina player.

"Lamine is a great player, and I follow him a lot because he plays for a club I love," he said humbly. "I always wish him all the best, no doubts that he’s among the best in the world. We’ll try to play a great match, but I hope he and his team don’t have their best day."

Even Messi acknowledges that the pair's unlikely reunion defies all logic, stating: "That picture with Lamine, it’s something crazy. Life is full of surprises! Now we are facing each other in a final after a photo was taken of us when he was a baby, it’s just insane!"

Article continues below

Now Yamal has the chance to steal Messi's thunder. Some may feel the script has already been written. Expect the unexpected, blink and you will miss it.

Sports.title: Argentina star faced 20,000-signature petition to dump girlfriend over World Cup final act
Sports.content:
Argentina star faced 20,000-signature petition to dump girlfriend over World Cup final act

A viral clip led to fans launching a petition calling for an Argentina World Cup hero to break up with his girlfriend

View 5 Images Julian Alvarez was urged to dump his girlfriend after the last World Cup (Image: Getty )

Julian Alvarez’s personal life was once the target of an extraordinary fan petition, with passionate Argentina supporters demanding he split from his stunning girlfriend. Alvarez played a key role for Argentina on Wednesday night, playing the full 90 minutes as they edged out England in a 2-1 World Cup semi-final victory.

‌



But while the Atletico Madrid striker was busy shattering English dreams on the pitch, it was his own relationship that fans previously tried to tear apart. The former Manchester City star has known Maria Emilia Ferrero—who goes by her middle name, Emilia—since their teenage years in Cordoba.

‌



However, the couple kept their relationship under wraps for years, only going public in 2022. The romance was only publicised after the forward's high-profile switch from River Plate to the Etihad, which saw Emilia uproot her life to join the striker in Manchester.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Lionel Messi bathes baby Lamine Yamal in weird throwback snaps ahead of World Cup final showdown READ MORE :

Lionel Messi takes advantage of FIFA rule vs England with double World Cup prize in sight READ MORE :

Alvarez truly burst into the global spotlight during the Qatar 2022 World Cup, netting four crucial goals to help Argentina end their 36-year wait for football's ultimate prize. Emilia was a constant source of support in the stands throughout the tournament, which gained her a massive social media following.

In the wake of their World Cup triumph, the pair headed back to their home city, where fans were understandably delighted to welcome their local hero. Alvarez had just finished dinner at Ferrero's family home in Cordoba when a group of young fans gathered outside and made a beeline for her boyfriend as the couple stepped out.

‌



5 View 5 Images Alvarez's girlfriend came under fire (Image: https://www.instagram.com/emiliafferrero/?hl=en) 5 View 5 Images Maria Emilia is a PE teacher (Image: instagram.com/emiliafferrero/)

Ferrero looked visibly annoyed and appeared to prevent them from taking pictures with Alvarez in a viral clip that quickly spread across social media. Her response, however, sparked fury among many of Alvarez's supporters online, with one fan taking things further by setting up a petition on Change.org demanding the footballer end their relationship.

‌



The petition quickly gained traction, attracting 20,000 signatures, which led former hockey player Ferrero to issue a statement on social media addressing the controversy. The 26-year-old attempted to explain her actions, revealing that several of the fans were actually her school pupils and that she was merely trying to organise a collective group photo with Alvarez, rather than several individual selfies.

Unsurprisingly, the then-City star completely ignored the petition. Instead, their connection has only deepened, with Ferrero following her partner to Spain after his £81million transfer to Atletico Madrid in 2024.

5 View 5 Images Maria Emilia loves to pose in bikinis (Image: Maria Emilia) 5 View 5 Images Ferrero has been cheering on her partner at the World Cup (Image: Maria Emilia Ferrero)

‌



Her social media presence has expanded considerably since then, now possessing 791,000 followers on Instagram. Most of her content centres around her life as a mother, supporting Alvarez at matches, gym selfies and eye-catching bikini photos.

Earlier this year, the pair celebrated the arrival of their first child together, a son named Amadeo, who was born on January 2. Ferrero and baby Amadeo made the journey to North America to cheer on Alvarez this summer.

Emilia wrote in one recent social media post: "Nuestro primer mundial juntos," which translates to "Our first World Cup together," before expressing how proud she was of the striker on Wednesday.

Article continues below

The family of three are set to relocate once more this summer amid reports linking Alvarez to a potential switch to either Barcelona or Arsenal. Alvarez, whose only goal at this World Cup came against Switzerland, announced that he informed Atletico of his desire to leave the club earlier in the tournament.

Sports.title: World Cup supercomputer issues prediction for Spain vs Argentina final
Sports.content:
World Cup supercomputer issues prediction for Spain vs Argentina final

Spain and Argentina will meet in the World Cup final on Sunday night

A supercomputer has predicted that Spain will win the World Cup. La Roja will face Argentina in the showpiece game in New Jersey's MetLife Stadium on Sunday.

‌



The Opta computer has calculated that the Spanish have a 45.1 per cent chance of winning the trophy for the second time in their history, inside 90 minutes.

‌



Argentina, the reigning champions, have been given a 29.4 per cent chance of victory. The probability of the World Cup final going to extra time, or even to a penalty shootout, stands at 25.4 per cent.

‌



Luis de la Fuente's side are slight favourites with a number of bookmakers heading into the tie. Spain outplayed France, many people's favourites to lift the World Cup this summer, with a comprehensive 2-0 win in the Semi-finals.

After beating Les Bleus, Manchester City and Spain midfielder Rodri said: "I’m very proud of my team and what it represents for us. Now it’s time to rest because we probably have the most important match of our lives on Sunday.

Jude Bellingham mocked by Enzo Fernandez's brother ahead of possible Real Madrid reunion READ MORE :

"We all needed each other. I had a lot of help in the midfield to control such a physical and aggressive team on second balls – I would say it was a very complete match."

‌



A Lionel Messi-inspired Argentina overcame England in their semi-final, coming from behind to win 2-1 in the dying stages of the game. If Messi, as expected, will feature against Spain, he will become only the second player, after Brazilian icon Cafu, to play in three World Cup finals after featuring in 2014 and 2022.

Victory over the Euro 2024 champions would also see the 39-year-old become the first captain to retain the World Cup, following Argentina's victory over France in Qatar four years ago.

View 3 Images Rodri is one game away from winning the World Cup (Image: Ulrik Pedersen/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

‌



Speaking after the famous win over the Three Lions, Messi said: "It was a special match against England, we couldn't lose. While this group doesn't owe anything to anyone, you know how Argentinians are, we always demand more.

"I think if we had lost today, people would have come out and said some nonsense, and we didn't give them the chance. We knew that we were better than them in terms of football.

"But a lot is at stake in a match of this magnitude, where historic events happen in these games, but it's still special because of everything it represents, and we had to win."

‌



Messi added: "Everything we experienced was incredible, from the very beginning, as we said. Although it was a football match, when we started to enter the field and during the anthem, we experienced special feelings, and the group felt that.

View 3 Images Lionel Messi of Argentina celebrates after the first goal scored by Enzo Fernandez (not in the picture) during the FIFA World Cup 2026 Semi Final match between England and Argentina (Image: Getty)

"It wasn't just another victory; it was an important victory that the Argentine people wanted, and we wanted it too, and it put us in another World Cup final.

‌



"It's crazy to play two World Cup finals in a row. This group is incredible. Today we went looking for it again when things got tough, we never stopped believing, never stopped trying.

"With our style of play, today we really put our game into it when we were down on the scoreboard. We pinned them back in their own half and it's an enormous joy."

Sports.title: Tokaido takes on two in the Prix Robert Papin
Sports.content:
We have a busy day’s racing on Sunday with action from Newton Abbot and Chantilly, live on Sky Sports Racing...

12.58 Chantilly - Tokaido faces King Of Cloughan and Beibhinn

A classy field of three head to post for this Group Two Prix Robert Papin at Chantilly.

Amy Murphy saddles Tokaido who recorded a third success on his fourth outing when comfortably claiming the Group Three Prix du Bois under Tony Piccone. That was his first try at six-furlongs and his connections are expecting him to handle this step up in class.

Joseph O'Brien is double handed with King Of Cloughan the pick. A son of St Mark's Basilica, he built on his first couple of starts to take the Windsor Castle Stakes at the Royal meeting. Only on top late on, he will appreciate a decent pace here under new rider Pierre-Charles Boudot.

Beibhinn landed a Listowel maiden on her second start before an excellent third in this grade at the Curragh so cannot be discounted.

4.35 Chantily - Exciting Erdenali bids to remain unbeaten

Erdenali looks to extend his winning run in an excellent Group Three Prix Messidor at 4.35pm.

Francis-Henri Graffard's gelding is unbeaten in all three starts having burst onto the scene at Saint-Cloud back in March. He takes another step up the ladder here but could prove equal to the test and remains a highly promising prospect.

Christopher Ferland's Silius is a solid yardstick who has claimed silver on his last two starts at this level so must be feared if in similar spirits.

Dark Trooper and Familly complete the shortlist.

5.22 Newton Abbot - Prolific pair No More No and Edgewell clash

In-form duo No More No and Edgewell lock horns in this closing Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Chase at Newton Abbot.

Lawney Hill's No More No returned from a layoff to make it two wins from two starts over fences and he makes appeal off a three-pound higher mark. Obviously not the easiest to train, he has been given time to recover from that outing.

Edgewell arrives in red-hot form having scored over this course and distance in June before claiming a Worcester handicap in game fashion last month. He enjoys quick ground and can give another bold showing.

The Grace Harris-trained My Girl Katie has won over this trip and track and cannot be ruled out.

Sports.title: England claim third at World Cup with win in 10-goal thriller over France
Sports.content:
Bukayo Saka’s hat-trick helped England to a remarkable 6-4 bronze medal win over France in Miami to achieve their best World Cup finish since 1966.

England were incredibly 4-0 up at half-time through Declan Rice's opener, Ezri Konsa's header and Saka's double, as Thomas Tuchel's side took advantage of an uninterested France - but they nearly blew their four-goal lead in the second half.

The two-time World Cup winners woke up after half-time to threaten a sensational comeback through Kylian Mbappe's double - which saw him become the World Cup's all-time leading scorer (22 goals) - and substitute Bradley Barcola's strike.
